bib.title: Text2SQL is Not Enough: Unifying AI and Databases with TAG

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Text2SQL is Not Enough: Unifying AI and Databases with TAG", Asim Biswal*, Liana Patel*, Siddharth Jha, Amog Kamsetty, Shu Liu, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Carlos Guestrin, Matei Zaharia (UC Berkeley, Stanford). arXiv:2408.14717v1 [cs.DB], 27 Aug 2024, preprint (short position paper plus small benchmark).

COVERAGE: 46283 of 46283 chars read, all 10 pages: body, tables, references and appendices A-C (sample queries, prompts, hand-written LOTUS pipelines). Nothing skipped. The extraction was clean. Table 1 columns are readable. Figure 1 text is jumbled but understandable.

CLAIMS
1. TAG is a three-step paradigm: Text2SQL and RAG are special cases of it.
 - number: 3 steps (syn, exec, gen)
 - setup: conceptual definition. It is defined as a single iteration, and multi-hop or agentic extension is left to future work.
 - quote: "First, the query synthesis step syn translates the user's arbitrary natural language request R to an executable database query Q. Then, the query execution step exec executes Q on the database system to efficiently compute the relevant data T. Lastly, the answer generation step gen utilizes R and T, where the LM is orchestrated, possibly in iterative or recursive patterns over the data, to generate the final natural language answer A." Also: "Notably, the TAG model unifies prior methods, including both Text2SQL and RAG, which represent special cases of TAG"
 - where: p1-2 (Sec 1, Eqs 1-3)
2. Standard baselines never exceed 20% exact match.
 - number: Text2SQL 0.17, RAG 0.00, Retrieval+LM Rank 0.02, Text2SQL+LM 0.13 overall
 - setup: 80 modified BIRD queries, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. Overall excludes aggregation queries because accuracy is not measured there. Exact match against human-labeled answers.
 - quote: "Text2SQL 0.17 5.63 0.20 4.72 0.20 4.01 0.10 7.26 N/A 6.53 / RAG 0.00 3.23 ... / Retrieval + LM Rank 0.02 4.82 ... / Text2SQL + LM 0.13 9.08 ..." and "never surpassing 20% exact match on the benchmark"
 - where: Table 1, p4; Sec 1
3. Hand-written TAG gets 55% overall, the best method.
 - number: 0.55 overall, with match 0.60, comparison 0.65, ranking 0.40
 - setup: hand-written LOTUS pipelines written with expert knowledge of the schema, not automatic query synthesis. Same 80-query benchmark.
 - quote: "Hand-written TAG 0.55 2.94 0.60 1.70 0.65 5.05 0.40 2.50 N/A 2.50" and "Our hand-written TAG baseline answers 55% of queries correctly overall, performing best on comparison queries with an exact match accuracy of 65%."
 - where: Table 1; Sec 4.3
4. The accuracy gain over baselines is 20-65 points. This is absolute percentage points, and the abstract and conclusion word it loosely as "higher accuracy".
 - number: 20% to 65%
 - quote: "Overall, this method gives us between a 20% to 65% accuracy improvement over the standard baselines."
 - where: Sec 4.3, p4
5. Plain RAG answered zero queries, and adding LM rerank answered one.
 - number: 0.00, with 10 rows retrieved
 - setup: row-level embeddings serialized "- col: val", E5 base, FAISS, top 10 rows. Rerank used Llama-3.1-70B scoring 0-1.
 - quote: "it fails to answer a single query correctly across all query types" and "Adding LM reranking allows Retrieval + LM rank to answer a query correctly among the comparison queries"
 - where: Sec 4.2-4.3
6. Text2SQL does worst on reasoning queries. Text2SQL+LM hits context-length errors.
 - number: Text2SQL 0.10 on reasoning and 0.10 on ranking. Text2SQL+LM 0.10 on match and comparison.
 - quote: "vanilla Text2SQL especially struggles on queries requiring LM reasoning with 10% exact match accuracy, due to its omission of the answer generation step." Also "several context length errors occur trying to feed in many rows to the model after the executed SQL."
 - where: Sec 4.3; Table 2
7. TAG exceeds 50% on both knowledge and reasoning queries.
 - number: Knowledge 0.53, Reasoning 0.60 (Text2SQL 0.20/0.10, RAG 0.00/0.00, Retr+Rank 0.03/0.00, Text2SQL+LM 0.10/0.20)
 - quote: "Hand-written TAG 0.53 3.50 0.60 2.24"
 - where: Table 2, p4
8. The TAG pipelines were also fast: up to 3.1x lower execution time.
 - number: 3.1x lower, 2.94 s average
 - setup: batched LM inference via the LOTUS engine, 8x A100 80GB with vLLM. No per-method breakdown beyond Table 1. TAG comparison ET is 5.05 s, the slowest of the TAG cells and slower than RAG's 2.29 s.
 - quote: "the hand-written TAG method offers an efficient implementation with up to 3.1× lower execution time over other baselines. The hand-written baseline takes an average of 2.94 seconds for all queries."
 - where: Sec 4.3
9. Aggregation queries are only qualitative. RAG retrieves only some of the relevant rows. Text2SQL+LM used only parametric knowledge.
 - number: none (Sepang circuit example)
 - quote: "The RAG baseline is only able to provide information about some of the races, as most of the relevant races are not retrieved." and "We leave quantitative analysis to future work."
 - where: Fig 2, Sec 4.3
10. Why RAG falls short, in the authors' framing: it does point lookups and leaves exact computation to the LM.
 - quote: "RAG model is limited to simple relevance-based point lookups to a few data records, followed by a single LM invocation... leaves computational tasks (e.g., counting, math and filtering) to a single invocation of the error-prone LM."
 - where: Sec 1

BENCHMARK SETUP (needed to cite any number)
- "Our final benchmark consists of 80 modified queries, 40 requiring parametric knowledge and 40 requiring reasoning, with 20 of each of the 4 chosen BIRD query types."
- The query types are match-based, comparison, ranking and aggregation. Aggregation is not scored.
- Five BIRD DBs: california_schools, debit_card_specializing, formula_1, codebase_community, european_football_2.
- Metric is exact match against human-labeled ground truth.
- Each cell of Table 1 therefore rests on about 20 queries (or fewer per knowledge/reasoning split). Differences of 5% equal one query.
- Text2SQL prompt: all table schemas in the BIRD format.

LIMITS
- Hand-written TAG is expert-written per query with knowledge of the schema. It does not test automatic query synthesis, so the 55% is an upper-bound-style demo, not a TAG system result.
- Tiny benchmark (80 queries, about 20 per cell), one model (Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct), one run. No variance or confidence intervals.
- Aggregation not measured quantitatively. The authors defer it to future work.
- The baselines are weak and untuned: RAG retrieves only 10 rows, and Text2SQL uses a plain BIRD prompt. No agentic or iterative baselines.
- TAG is defined as a single iteration. Multi-hop and agentic loops are future work.
- The authors are LOTUS authors, so there is a conflict of interest: the winning method is their own system.
- Typo in the paper: Appendix B says "Llama-3.1 80B" while the body says 70B.
- Dated: 2024 models and a Llama-3.1 evaluation. Later TAG work is not covered.

BUILDS ON
- BIRD (Li et al. 2023) for the benchmark.
- LOTUS (Patel, Jha, Guestrin, Zaharia 2024) semantic operators: sem_filter, sem_topk, sem_agg.
- RAG (Lewis et al. 2021).
- Table retrieval: Herzig et al. 2021 (dense table retrieval); Chen, Zhang, Roth 2024 (join-aware).
- STaRK (Wu et al. 2024) for LM reranking.
- SUQL (Liu et al. 2024).
- LM UDFs in SQL (Liu et al. 2024, Optimizing LLM Queries in Relational Workloads); Liu et al. 2024 declarative AI system.
- Text2SQL line: Zelle & Mooney 1996, SQLizer 2017, Seq2SQL 2017, Spider 2019, WikiSQL, TypeSQL 2018.
- Tools: FAISS (Douze et al. 2024), E5 (Wang et al. 2024), vLLM (Kwon et al. 2023).
- Spider2-V (Cao et al. 2024) for agentic data assistants.
- Motivation drawn from Databricks customer and internal workloads (no numbers given).

CODE (Appendix C, p9-10; extraction mangled spacing)
- Match-based: `sv_cities = unique_cities.sem_filter("{ City } is a city in the Silicon Valley region ")`
- Ranking: `posts_df.sem_topk("What { Title } is most technical ?", 5)`
- Aggregation: `merged_df.sem_agg("Summarize the comments", all_cols=True)`
- Pattern: pandas filter or sort first for exact work, then a semantic operator on the small result.
- Answer-generation prompt (App B.2): "Your answer must be a list of values that is evaluatable in Python. Respond in the format [value1, value2, ... , valueN]."

FIGURES
- Fig 1, p2: the TAG pipeline with a movies example ("Summarize the reviews of the highest grossing romance movie considered a 'classic'"). It shows the three stages and the LM-as-filter inside SQL. The clearest one-glance explanation.
- Fig 2, p4: Sepang circuit aggregation outputs for RAG, Text2SQL+LM and hand-written TAG.
- Figure extraction script was not run. Captions above come from the text extraction.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Figure 1 text is scrambled in the extraction. The Table 1 header is partly garbled, but the values are unambiguous. A previous tool call was truncated, and I re-read the remainder (chars 39500 to end).
